correctness.rationale: Each species absence event has exact probability C(N-a,k)/C(N,k), giving an integer numerator whose comparisons preserve sign. Every census abundance multiset is exactly an integer partition; the largest-part recursion enumerates all partitions once, and all unordered pairs for N=1..16 are checked with exact integer comparisons at all k. A separately coded part-frequency generator agrees on every partition set. Zero double-switch pairs occur through N=15; at N=16 exactly two of 26,565 pairs qualify. Each witness is independently checked via all 65,536 labeled subsets, with exact sample richness totals. This proves only discrete equal-census hypergeometric claims.

originality.rationale: The existing literature states and studies single or multiple rarefaction-curve crossings and provides the hypergeometric formula. The new exact statement is the smallest common integer census total permitting two strict sign switches at integer sample sizes, N=16, with exactly two unordered boundary abundance partitions. The full inspected 2001 comparison text states that curves may cross twice but does not give the sharp minimum or boundary-pair classification; the 2000 paper analyzes a different (with-replacement) model and does not imply this result. No matching classification was recovered from actual targeted public searches, selected indexed mathematical-record searches, or accessible prior local claims. Some potentially relevant complete sources remain uninspected; originality is not externally certified.
residual_risks: Unindexed or uncatalogued exact finite rarefaction partition enumeration could already identify the same sharp size and witnesses.
The complete Heck (1975) and Chao et al. (2014) texts were not read; author metadata and partial descriptions cannot exclude all appendices.
The result applies only to discrete sampling without replacement; comparisons in related asymptotic, replacement, or coverage-standardized models need not agree.

value.rationale: Rarefaction comparisons are an established tool for conservation diversity ranking; prior ecological literature notes that rank order can reverse twice with sample size. The unknown sharp smallest integer census and complete list of first-attaining abundance distributions constitute a natural, exactly defined finite complexity threshold for this practical comparison ambiguity. The identified 16-individual boundary and only two extremal pairs explain when early and complete richness rankings can agree while an intermediate richness ranking contradicts both. No empirical impact or broad inferential theorem is claimed.
